bias: 'Friday's liquidation, the buyer's exit, and the battle for control of the lower distribution.' Friday's open was a spectacular selloff that looked like a liquidation break (late Wed/Thu longs stopped out with the big buyer gone) rather than sustained initiative selling: once the initial liquidation finished, sellers made little further progress, and after the LBAF of the IB low (the low of day) a persistent buy program turned on, pulling value higher into the close instead of leaving a clean b-shaped profile. 'A significant buyer exiting the market is not the same thing as a significant seller entering it.' Weekly frame unchanged: NQ failed its upper distribution and finished in the lower one (above 28200-28233 = upper, below 28096-28129 = lower, between = transition where he expects sellers to try to establish control — an expectation, not a prediction); ES sits inside one big balance 7490-7504 to 7670-7680; neither has resolved the Nov 5 mother bar. Friday's decline didn't even retrace 50% of the rally — a reasonable pullback where responsive buyers could emerge; 'equally premature to become overly bearish on the first meaningful pullback.' Monday's job: distinguish genuine initiative from temporary liquidation.
wildcard: Futures sold off after Friday's cash close (FAA ground stop news): ES 5 PM 7561 in 7558-7563, NQ 5 PM 27927 just under 27953-27969 — both analyses start there. He evaluates each session with fresh eyes: an Asia excursion doesn't bind Europe/US. The LAAF-of-ARH shorts are structurally A-grade but discretionarily downgraded (NQ A-, ES B+) because Friday looked like liquidation and the afternoon buy program may return; reactive longs (dip holds above Friday's low → session uptrend) are implied but ungraded.
